saints.name: St. Bruno
saints.title: Priest and Founder
saints.shortBlurb: A learned master of Reims who fled fame for the silence of the mountains and founded the Carthusian Order…
biography: Born at Cologne about 1030, Bruno became a celebrated teacher at Reims, numbering a future pope among his pupils. Repelled by ecclesiastical corruption and drawn to solitude, he withdrew with a few companions into the wild valley of the Chartreuse near Grenoble in 1084, founding there the first Carthusian hermitage.

Called to Rome to advise Pope Urban II, he declined a bishopric and instead established a second charterhouse in Calabria, where he died in 1101. The order he founded, uniting the hermit's solitude with a common life, is famed for never having required reform.

canonization.canonized: Cultus approved 1514 by Pope Leo X; feast extended to the whole Church 1623
